nodes.summary: A root sufficiently close to the approximation has the same derivative valuation.
nodes.title: Nearby roots share the derivative valuation

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ and normalized additive valuation $v \colon A \to \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. If $d \in A$ is nonzero and $q \in \mathfrak{m}$, then $v(d) < v(d) + v(q)$.
nodes.title: Elements of the maximal ideal have positive valuation

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with normalized additive valuation $v \colon A \to \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. For every polynomial $p \in A[X]$ and all $a, a_0 \in A$, we have $v(a - a_0) \le v(p(a) - p(a_0))$.
nodes.title: Polynomials do not decrease the valuation of differences

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with normalized additive valuation $v \colon A \to \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, let $f \in A[X]$ have derivative $f'$, and let $a_0 \in A$. If $a, a' \in A$ are roots of $f$ with $v(f'(a_0)) < v(a - a_0)$ and $v(f'(a_0)) < v(a' - a_0)$, then $a = a'$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of roots near a point

nodes.summary: Over a Henselian local ring, an étale algebra has a section lifting any residue-field point.
nodes.title: Sections of étale algebras over Henselian local rings

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ that is complete and Hausdorff for the $\mathfrak{m}$-adic topology, and let $v \colon A \to \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ be its normalized additive valuation. Let $f \in A[X]$ have derivative $f'$, and let $a_0 \in A$ satisfy $2 v(f'(a_0)) < v(f(a_0))$. Then $f$ has a root $a \in A$ such that $a - a_0 \in \mathfrak{m}$,…
nodes.title: Hensel's lemma with a derivative bound

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ that is complete and Hausdorff for the $\mathfrak{m}$-adic topology. Let $f \in A[X]$ have derivative $f'$, and let $a_0 \in A$ satisfy $f(a_0) \in \mathfrak{m}$ with $f'(a_0)$ a unit of $A$. Then $f$ has a root $a \in A$ with $a - a_0 \in \mathfrak{m}$.
nodes.title: Hensel's lemma for complete discrete valuation rings

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I$ an ideal of $A$ such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete and $A/I$ is not the zero ring, and let $f \in A[X]$ be monic. Suppose the reduction of $f$ modulo $I$ equals $\bar g \bar h$, where $\bar g, \bar h \in (A/I)[X]$ are monic and coprime (that is, $a \bar g + b \bar h = 1$ for some $a, b \in (A/I)[X]$). Then there exist monic $g, h \in A[X]$ with $f = gh$ whose reductions…
nodes.title: Hensel lifting of monic coprime factorizations, with degrees

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I$ an ideal of $A$ such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete, and let $f \in A[X]$ be monic. Suppose the reduction of $f$ modulo $I$ equals $\bar g \bar h$, where $\bar g, \bar h \in (A/I)[X]$ are monic and coprime (that is, $a \bar g + b \bar h = 1$ for some $a, b \in (A/I)[X]$). Then there exist monic $g, h \in A[X]$ with $f = gh$ whose reductions modulo $I$ are $\bar g$ and…
nodes.title: Hensel lifting of monic coprime factorizations

nodes.summary: Coprime monic factors lift over a ring complete at the kernel of a surjective homomorphism. The lifts are coprime, and the first is the unique monic divisor of the original polynomial with its specified reduction.
nodes.title: Hensel lifting of coprime monic factors over a complete ring

nodes.summary: A monic factor of a coprime factorization lifts uniquely through a surjective homomorphism with nilpotent kernel. The original polynomial and the complementary reduced factor are not required to be monic.
nodes.title: Unique lift of a monic factor through a nilpotent-kernel surjection

nodes.summary: A valuation subring of an algebraically closed field is Henselian.
nodes.title: Valuation subrings of algebraically closed fields are Henselian

nodes.summary: A local ring homomorphism reflects coprimality of polynomials when the first polynomial is monic. Neither ring needs to be local.
nodes.title: Local homomorphisms reflect coprimality with a monic polynomial

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. If $R$ is Hausdorff and complete for the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology, then $R$ is a Henselian local ring.
nodes.title: Complete local rings are Henselian

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
